newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ central bank says market easing has gone too far.
newsitem.headline: NZ central bank says market easing has gone too far.

text.p: New Zealand's Reserve Bank governor stepped into the monetary policy ring on Thursday and told the country's financial markets that a combination of a lower currency and flat interest rates seen in recent days meant the market had eased too far and should retrace its steps.

In a short statement, Governor Don Brash reiterated that desired monetary conditions -- as measured by an index combining 90-day bank bill rates and the kiwi dollar -- had not changed since Friday's release of the Bank's Monetary Policy Statement.
"Conditions have eased too far," the central bank said.
Its present yardstick is 825 on its Monetary Conditions Index (MCI), and the bank has said it can accommodate a movement of 50 basis points on either side of that average.
During Wednesday and again on Thursday a weakening New Zealand dollar took the MCI down to a low point near 748 ahead of the statement -- more than 75 basis points below optimum.

"Against this background, actual monetary conditions have been too easy over recent days. We will be looking to see actual conditions settle closer to the announced desired levels," Brash said in the statement.

The kiwi dollar rebounded 21 points on its Trade Weighted Index, a basket which reflects the proportion of key export currencies in New Zealand's trade balance, within 20 minutes of Brash's statement in what currency dealers said was a reasonably muted response.
"It is not an excessively large upward movement yet," ANZ Investment Bank's head of foreign exchange Bill Murdoch said when the TWI was up 14 points.
Before the RBNZ announcement the TWI was at 66.28, but rose towards 66.50 before retracing lower to around 66.3.
Murdoch said the RBNZ had given a clear indication of what it wanted and although it reacted when the MCI was down about 75 points he did not expect it to come in at that point every time.
"It is a clear signal the markets should take heed of.
"Most of the downward pressure on the MCI has been because of the (kiwi) dollar," Murdoch said.
"There has been a bit of disinvestment out of the NZ dollar over the last 24 hours or so and that is making the retracement in the kiwi-U.S. a little more muted," he added.
At the same time as the kiwi tried to rally and interest rates edged up slightly to address some of the bank's concerns, share prices bounded ahead to fresh highs.

Continuing a rally spurred by last week's Monetary Policy Statement, which sanctioned a 100 basis point easing in conditions, the NZ Top 40 index surged during midsession trade to a new high of nearly 2515 points, narrowly above its record close from Monday.
